title: AI vs 1,076 human traders: the results
author: Mr_Hodlerr
selftext:
**Head to head**

\- The AI made more money than 844 of them (78%).

\- The AI had the smaller worst drop against 1,007 (94%).

\- 26 traders (2.4%) beat it on both return and worst drop.

\- Made money: traders 31%, the AI 89%.



**What it would have changed for the losing side**  


For the 844 traders the AI out-earned, here's their real result next to the AI's on the same dates:



\- Ended in a loss: 87% of the traders vs 10% with the AI

\- $10,000 became $4,395 vs $12,475

\- Typical worst drop: 100% vs 19%



**The pattern behind it**

Its edge in this test wasn't bigger wins. The difference was the size of the drops.

That shows up in the humans too. 71% of traders whose worst drop stayed under 25% made money. Of the ones who lost 90% at some point, 9% did.

That's where I think AI actually helps retail. Not by predicting better than a good trader, but by following the same rules on its worst day as on its best. No revenge trades, no sizing up after a loss.



**Questions**

\- Where do you think AI really helps retail traders: finding better trades or just keeping the losses small?

\- Would you let an AI trade your account or only use it as a second opinion?  


Full report with the method, tables and bot check: [https://botsfolio.com/blog/ai-vs-human-traders](https://botsfolio.com/blog/ai-vs-human-traders)

comments.author: Dependent-Ocelot908
comments.body: I had a similar finding, AI worked better to reduce loss than to make profit or find a good trade.

replies.author: Mr_Hodlerr
replies.body: So whats your thought, if most retail started using AI to reduce the drops then will the top 1% make less money or will the market behaviour change?

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: I think the honest answer is keeping losses small, which matches what your data shows. The big thing to check is how the comparison was built: the AI's results come from the company's own system, so I'd want to know if they're live or simulated and whether the human traders were similar accounts (size, time period, market). I'd only use it as a second opinion until it has months of live results with fees. Cymetica lets you connect your own AI agent and run it in paper mode first, which is a safer way to test one.
